name: Jimi (Cameroon)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Jimi (Cameroon) is not in the catalog and the sweep surfaced one title, Gravina 2012 'Vowels, consonants and prosody in two Central Chadic languages' (Jimi and Sharwa), a chapter in the Köppe WOCAL 6 proceedings (pp. 245-258 per the publisher TOC at DNB; Glottolog's '7-20' looks wrong). No open copy exists: no DOI, no scan at Open Library/archive.org, not in the SIL archives (Gravina's 2015 SIL contributor listing has 18 items, none this one; SIL item 8934 'The Phonology of Two Central Chadic Languages' is Smith & Gravina 2010 on Muyang/Mbuko, a different work), and OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/Google Books/most search engines were rate-limited or blocked from our machine. 'Prosody' here is the Central Chadic palatalization/labialization sense; the same author's 2014 thesis treats Jimi/Sharwa consonants, vowels and the palatalization prosody and states twice that tone and stress are not treated, and Yee 2021 (already on file) describes Jimi as a two-level lexical-tone language with no mention of stress. Relevance: prosody-but-not-word-stress; priority low. No first-hand statement on Jimi word stress was read; best_new_statement found=false. fetched sources records and the audit trail are in ( appended).

new_statements.quote: According to the most recent updates, which are summarized in Table 1 and 2, the sound system consists of seven vowels, which are expressed as six vowel symbols in the proposed orthography, 30 consonants, two levels of lexical tone, as well as an expansive use of the processes of labialization and palatalization. [...] At this point, there is no evidence for grammatical tone in Jimi, but Boyd (2021) has identified two contrastive levels of high and low tone lexically, making four possible tonal melodies within words. She also identified a middle level found in some verbal derivations as well as in phrase-final position. [p. 12:] Monosyllabic verb roots are lexically either low tone or high tone.
new_statements.citation: Yee, Shannon. 2021. Linkers and the Jimi Verb Phrase. M.A. essay, Wayne State University (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 92110), sec. 1.2.1 Phonology.
new_statements.locator: sec. 1.2.1, p. 7 (PDF p. 8); also p. 12 (PDF p. 13)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Jimi is described as a tone language with two contrastive lexical tone levels (H, L) and word-level palatalization/labialization prosodies; neither Yee 2021 nor Gravina 2014 (sec. 6.2) says anything about word stress or accent, so no stress rule is on record.
new_statements.exceptions: none (a phonetic mid level in some verbal derivations and phrase-finally is noted for tone, not stress)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement is word-level lexical tone; Yee explicitly leaves tone out of her transcription and defers to Boyd 2021 (unpublished) for the phonology; no stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Jimi of the Bourrah (Bourrha) subdivision, Mayo-Tsanaga, Far North Cameroon (self-name Jimjimen/Majimen; ALCAM 211) = Glottolog jimi1254 / ISO jim. Not to be confused with Jimi of Nigeria [jmi] (jimi1255), a different Chadic language. Gravina 2014 treats Jimi jointly with Sharwa [swq] in one case study but keeps the data separate.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.2.1 Phonology (p. 7) summarizes Boyd 2021 ms.: 7 vowels, 30 consonants, two levels of lexical tone (H, L; four word melodies; a mid level in some verbal derivations and phrase-finally), labialization/palatalization prosodies, no grammatical tone; p. 12: monosyllabic verb roots lexically L or H. The word 'stress' occurs only as a verb (p. ~17).

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic (LOT 375). Leiden University PhD dissertation. Sec. 6.2 'Case Study - Jimi and Sharwa', pp. 134-143.
sources.note: Nothing on Jimi stress; segmental inventory, labialized/palatalized consonants, three underlying vowels /a ə i/ (+ long iː aː), completive palatalization prosody. Author states (p. 1 and Section III intro) that tone and stress are not treated ('No attempt has been made to reconstruct tone or stress'). Jimi data from Djibi n.d. Dictionnaire Jimi and own fieldwork.
